title: LLM structured output: preserve response_format through fallback
h1: LLM structured output: preserve response_format through fallback
description: Preserve the original response_format contract across LLM fallback, reject adapters that cannot honor it before SDK calls, and distinguish JSON mode from schema enforcement.
summary: An adapter that accepts response_format but drops it can silently turn a structured request into free text. Fallback must preserve the same output contract or explicitly refuse the request.

review.author: API Atlas
review.distinctProblem: An adapter that accepts response_format but drops it can silently turn a structured request into free text. Fallback must preserve the same output contract or explicitly refuse the request.

sections.symptoms: A primary adapter rejects or cannot implement a structured-output request, and a fallback returns plain text because the format argument disappeared. In the reviewed revision, the common factory forwards `response_format`; unsupported adapters reject it before their SDK is called. The observed application error text is `provider does not support response_format`, not a vendor error message. The dependency lock pins `openai==2.46.0`.
sections.cause: A common method signature is not proof that each adapter implements every parameter. The reviewed regression asserts that an unsupported Anthropic adapter makes no SDK call and that the OpenAI fallback receives the original format object. This concerns those application wrappers; it does not establish that Anthropic or Gemini APIs generally lack structured-output features. The [official OpenAI guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=chat) distinguishes JSON mode from schema-constrained output.
sections.verification:
Synthetic Python examples were checked on 2026-10-16; the original application tests and live provider APIs were not run.

Pass a single format object such as {'type': 'json_object'} and assert the fallback transport receives that exact object. Assert zero calls for an unsupported adapter, preserve the contract when a supported primary times out, and reject a text result rather than accepting silent degradation. If all adapters are unsupported, fail without making a provider call. Invalid format types must fail before any transport.

The checked-in tests extract this published Python block and exercise the same synthetic boundary cases. Re-run with `npm test`.
sections.limitations:
A json_object fixture proves argument preservation and a parsed-object boundary; it does not prove strict JSON Schema adherence, every required business field, or live model compliance. A strict-schema requirement needs an explicitly supported adapter plus local validation; refusals and truncated responses remain separate outcomes. The example does not translate between different vendors' schema dialects or migrate Chat Completions response_format to Responses text.format. See the [LLM selection guide](../choose-llm-api/) and [Anthropic profile](../../apis/anthropic/).
